old: A shouted challenge from {a} ({af}) reached {b} ({bf}) at {place}. The answer was lost beneath the guns. The challenge was not repeated.
new: {a} ({af}) shouted a challenge across to {b} ({bf}) at {place}. The answer was lost under the guns. Nobody repeated the challenge.

old: {a} of the {af} spotted {b} of the {bf} repairing a parapet at {place}. A warning shot brought the repair to an abrupt halt.
new: {a} of the {af} spotted {b} of the {bf} repairing a parapet at {place}. A warning shot stopped the repair on the spot.

old: A bucket appeared above the {bf} parapet at {place}. {a} fired; {b} pulled the bucket down. A sign later appeared: 'Water costs enough already.'
new: A bucket appeared above the {bf} parapet at {place}. {a} fired. {b} pulled the bucket down. Later a sign went up: 'Water costs enough already.'

old: A splinter opened {name}'s cheek at {sector}. A medic stitched it in the bay and {he} was back on the fire step before the tea went cold.
new: A splinter opened {name}'s cheek at {sector}. A medic stitched it on the spot and {he} was back on the fire step before the tea went cold.

old: Blast from a trench mortar threw {name} against the revetment at {sector}. Ringing ears, a split lip, and no intention of leaving.
new: Blast from a trench mortar threw {name} against the trench wall at {sector}. Ringing ears, a split lip, and no intention of leaving.

old: A trench mortar bomb landed in the next bay. The blast caught {name} at {sector} and the bearers came at a run.
new: A trench mortar bomb landed in the next section of trench. The blast caught {name} at {sector} and the bearers came at a run.

old: A shell burst in the bay at {sector}. {name} was thrown against the revetment and did not get up. The bearers came at a run.
new: A shell burst in the trench at {sector}. {name} was thrown against the wall and did not get up. The bearers came at a run.

old: A direct hit on the bay at {sector}. {name} was the only one they could still help, and only just.
new: A direct hit on the trench at {sector}. {name} was the only one they could still help, and only just.

old: Stand-to at dawn. {name} put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: {target}, {how}.
new: Dawn watch. {name} put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: {target}, {how}.

old: {name} fired twice at the enemy sap. The second shot found {target}, {how}. Nobody in the bay said anything.
new: {name} fired twice at the enemy sap. The second shot found {target}, {how}. Nobody nearby said anything.

old: There was no bed for {name}. {He} lay on a stretcher outside, wrapped in a greatcoat, listening to the guns.
new: There was no bed for {name}. {He} lay on a stretcher outside, wrapped in a coat, listening to the guns.

old: {name} opened {his} eyes today and asked for water. In the {sector} bay they cheered when the news came up the line.
new: {name} opened {his} eyes today and asked for water. At {sector} they cheered when the news came up the line.

old: There was no room for {name}. {He} died in the night under a borrowed greatcoat, a few yards from a bed that never came free.
new: There was no room for {name}. {He} died in the night under a borrowed coat, a few yards from a bed that never came free.

old: {name} volunteered for a supply run to headquarters. {He} came back with exactly what was ordered and a suspiciously large greatcoat.
new: {name} volunteered for a supply run to headquarters. {He} came back with exactly what was ordered and a suspiciously large coat.

why: zmínka o počasí v textu, který není o počasí
old: {name}'s diary, day nine: "Still here. Rain. A rat called the Major. Nothing else worth writing, which is the point."
new: {name}'s diary, day nine: "Still here. Soup again. A rat called the Major. Nothing else worth writing, which is the point."

old: The reply to {name}'s chess move arrived with a complaint about the weather at home. {His} opponent has taken a pawn and apologised for nothing.
new: The reply to {name}'s chess move arrived with a long complaint about the weather at home and a note that {his} opponent had taken a pawn.

old: {name} received a parcel meant for another soldier with the same surname. Inside were {gift}. {He} put everything back and kept the wrapping.
new: A parcel came for {name} that was really meant for another soldier with the same surname. Inside: {gift}. {He} put everything back and kept only the wrapping.

old: {name} caught a supply driver heading toward one of the units. The parcel went along with a note asking for word when it arrived.
new: {name} caught a supply driver heading for one of the units and handed the parcel over with a note asking for word when it arrived.

old: A card reached {name}: the parcel had found its owner. The message thanked {him} for returning {gift}, especially with the shortage at home.
new: A card reached {name}: the parcel had found its owner. The message said thank you, and that {gift} had come just in time.

old: {name} heard a faint second conversation on the telephone line. Headquarters insisted only one circuit was connected.
new: {name} heard a faint second conversation on the telephone line. Headquarters said only one line was connected.

old: The extra voice returned during {name}'s test. It was discussing potatoes, which made enemy intelligence seem an unlikely explanation.
new: The extra voice came back during {name}'s test. It was talking about potatoes, which made enemy spies an unlikely explanation.

old: {name} traced the fault to two poorly insulated wires pressed together near a junction. One belonged to the supply office.
new: {name} traced the fault to two badly insulated wires touching near a junction. One of them belonged to the supply office.

old: With the wires separated, {name}'s telephone carried only orders again. The section misses knowing in advance what is wrong with supper.
new: With the wires separated, {name}'s telephone carried only orders again. The section misses hearing what was for supper before it was served.

old: nobody, which {he} says is easier
new: a mother who sets a place for {him} at every meal

old: a dog called Bastion on the farm
new: an old neighbor who promised to keep {his} garden alive

old: {name} turned a year older today. The bay sang for {him}, badly, and the cook found a candle.
new: {name} turned a year older today. The whole squad sang for {him}, badly, and the cook found a candle.

old: {name} stood to at dawn with the rest of {sector}, bayonet fixed, staring into the grey. Nothing came. Nothing came yesterday, either.
new: {name} stood at the parapet at dawn with the rest of {sector}, bayonet fixed, staring into the grey. Nothing came. Nothing came yesterday, either.

old: {name} repaired a collapsed traverse at {sector} with sandbags, boards and language not fit for letters home.
new: {name} repaired a collapsed wall of the trench at {sector} with sandbags, boards and language not fit for letters home.

old: In the reserve billet {name} played football against the sappers. The ball was a sandbag stuffed with straw. The sappers cheated.
new: In the rear quarters, {name} played football against the sappers. The ball was a sandbag stuffed with straw. The sappers cheated.

old: The field hospital let {name} go. {He} came back up the line on foot because the lorry would not wait.
new: The field hospital let {name} go. {He} came back up the line on foot because the truck would not wait.

old: A white flag, a handshake in the mud, and {name} walked back across no man's land in an exchange of prisoners. The bay cheered {him} in.
new: A white flag, a handshake in the mud, and {name} walked back across no man's land in an exchange of prisoners. The whole squad cheered {him} in.

old: A shell landed square in the bay at {sector}. {name} was killed outright. The bearers found nothing to carry.
new: A shell landed square in the trench at {sector}. {name} was killed outright. The bearers found nothing to carry.

old: {name} fired twice at the enemy sap. The second shot found {target}, {how}. Nobody nearby said anything.
new: {name} fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found {target}, {how}. Nobody nearby said anything.

old: {pet} the rat now waits for {name} at stand-to every morning. {He} shares crumbs with it. The corporal calls this desertion of rations.
new: {pet} the rat now waits for {name} at dawn watch every morning. {He} shares crumbs with it. The corporal calls this desertion of rations.
